title: Component Lexicon & Microstate Kit for Compact Cost Widgets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, repeatable lexicon of components and explicit microstates for cost-related widgets in the Redwood Console. The goal is to reduce visual inconsistency across dashboards and rollout surfaces, improve density token decisions for small screens, and provide a Figma kit with naming conventions and usage rules for engineers and frontend owners.
acceptance_criteria: A shared Figma component library (compact/callout/mini-chart/inline-pill) published with semantic names
Microstate documentation covering idle/hover/focus/loading/error/overflow for each component
A token mapping table recommending spacing, type scale, and elevation tokens for three density tiers
Handoff notes (CSS class conventions and React component prop mapping) added to the library description
Design review sign-off from PM and Engineering UI owner
notes: This ticket consolidates several small pattern experiments that were applied inconsistently across the cost dashboard and rollout inspector surfaces. It aims to replace ad-hoc variants with a single source of truth and rationalized density tiers.
risks: If the lexicon is not adopted by feature owners, fragmentation will continue and front-end implementation time increases. The most significant technical risk is mapping Figma token names to existing CSS variables across two legacy component libraries.
decisions: Use semantic component names (compact-card, mini-sparkline, inline-cost-pill) rather than size-first names
Three density tiers: standard, compact, ultra-compact; each has explicit token mappings
Microstates include overflow behaviors and truncation rules for numeric displays to avoid layout shifts
